mainTopic: Making an עירוב with food the person cannot eat: בית שמאי and בית הלל, חנניה's view, סומכוס on תרומה and personal measures, and a כהן's עירוב in a בית הפרס or cemetery (אהל זרוק)
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא in which בית הלל argue with בית שמאי about making an עירוב with food the person himself cannot eat. בית שמאי admit that an עירוב works for an adult on יום הכפורים. They still reject wine for a נזיר and תרומה for a ישראל, because that food was never fit for them, even before the holy day began. The גמרא notes that this ברייתא does not follow חנניה. In חנניה's version, בית שמאי require a person to actually move his bed and belongings, and the גמרא uses that view to explain a ברייתא about black and white clothing. Next the גמרא explains סומכוס, who forbids a תרומה עירוב for a ישראל. After several attempts, it concludes that separating תרומה is a שבות that is already forbidden at בין השמשות, the moment the עירוב takes effect. רבי זירא shows that סומכוס is also behind the rule that the two-meal amount is measured by each person, but a glutton's huge appetite is ignored. Finally, the גמרא explains why a כהן may place his עירוב in a בית הפרס, and why רבי יהודה allows it even in a cemetery: a moving container (אהל זרוק) counts as a tent, a point on which תנאים disagree. The amud ends as the גמרא begins quoting another ברייתא from רבי יהודה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: בית הלל point to the יום הכפורים case
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל finish their challenge to בית שמאי. They ask whether בית שמאי agree that an עירוב may be made for an adult on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Don't you agree] that one may make an עירוב for an adult on יום הכפורים?!
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a question that בית הלל put to בית שמאי. They want בית שמאי to admit that an עירוב works for an adult on יום הכפורים, even though he may not eat on that day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי hold that an עירוב needs food the person himself can eat. בית הלל bring a case where the person cannot eat the food at all, yet everyone agrees the עירוב still works. If בית שמאי agree to this case, their rule about the נזיר and the ישראל becomes harder to defend.

keyTerms.meaning: We make an עירוב, here meaning placing food to set a new שבת home base for walking (עירוב תחומין)
An adult, who is obligated to fast
The Day of Atonement, a day when eating is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The opening words of בית הלל's question appear on the previous amud. Read this line as the end of the question 'Don't you agree...?'

phrases.english: that one may make an eiruv for an adult on Yom Kippur!
phrases.notes: End of בית הלל's question, which began with 'Don't you agree...'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא earlier, where בית הלל began questioning בית שמאי
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's position that an עירוב cannot be made with food the person himself cannot eat
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On יום הכפורים the adult cannot eat the food, yet the עירוב works. This suggests that being able to eat the food is not required.

steps.title: בית שמאי agree
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי admit that an עירוב may indeed be made for an adult on יום הכפורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to them: Yes, indeed.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי answer the question with a simple 'yes.' This sets up בית הלל's next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the word אבל means 'indeed' or 'yes.' It does not mean 'but.' Now that בית שמאי have agreed to the יום הכפורים case, בית הלל can use it as a model for the cases they are arguing about.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means 'indeed / yes,' not 'but'
They said to them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not translate אבל as 'but' here. In this ברייתא it means agreement: 'Yes, that is true.'

phrases.english: They (Beit Shammai) said to them: Indeed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי agree that an עירוב may be made for an adult on יום הכפורים

steps.title: בית הלל compare the נזיר and the ישראל to יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל argue that the agreed-upon יום הכפורים case shows an עירוב can also be made for a נזיר with wine and for a ישראל with תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to them: Just as one may make an עירוב for an adult on יום הכפורים, so too one may make an עירוב for a נזיר with wine and for a ישראל with תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל use the case בית שמאי just agreed to as a comparison. They argue it should apply equally to the נזיר and to the ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all three cases, the person himself may not eat the food. If that does not stop the עירוב on יום הכפורים, it should not stop it for a נזיר with wine or a ישראל with תרומה either. The challenge now puts pressure on בית שמאי to explain the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too, a comparison formula
A person who took a vow forbidding him to drink wine
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which a non-כהן (ישראל) may not eat
Wine

phrases.english: They (Beit Hillel) said to them:
Just as one may make an eiruv for an adult on Yom Kippur,
so too one may make an eiruv for a nazir with wine
and for an Israelite with teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמְּעָרְבִין לַגָּדוֹל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים, כֵּן מְעָרְבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on בית שמאי's admission in step 2 to push the challenge
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's ruling that an עירוב cannot be made for a נזיר with wine or for a ישראל with תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The יום הכפורים case, which everyone accepts, also involves food the person cannot eat. So the נזיר and ישראל cases should be treated the same way.

steps.title: בית שמאי's distinction: the food was fit while it was still day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how בית שמאי tell the cases apart. Before יום הכפורים began, the food was fit for the adult to eat. Wine for a נזיר and תרומה for a ישראל were never fit for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do בית שמאי answer? There, on יום הכפורים, there is a meal that was fit for him while it was still day. Here, there is no meal that was fit for him while it was still day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends בית שמאי by showing that the יום הכפורים case is different from the נזיר and ישראל cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב יום הכפורים, the adult was allowed to eat that food during the daytime, before the fast began. So the food was fit for him at some point. Wine for a נזיר and תרומה for a ישראל are forbidden to them all the time, even on ערב שבת, so they were never fit for them at all.

keyTerms.meaning: There, referring to the יום הכפורים case
Here, referring to the נזיר and ישראל cases
A meal that is fit to be eaten
While it is still day, before the holy day begins

steps.whatToRemember: According to בית שמאי, an עירוב works if the food was fit for the person at least before the holy day began. This is why the יום הכפורים case works, but a נזיר with wine and a ישראל with תרומה do not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives בית שמאי's real requirement: the food must have been fit for the person at some point. Food he can never eat does not qualify.

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai (how do they respond)?

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — אִיכָּא סְעוּדָה הָרְאוּיָה מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם,
phrases.english: There (Yom Kippur), there is a meal that was fit while it was still day,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא — לֵיכָּא סְעוּדָה הָרְאוּיָה מִבְּעוֹד יוֹם.
phrases.english: here (nazir/teruma), there is no meal that was fit while it was still day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the comparison בית הלל made in step 3
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the adult on יום הכפורים also cannot eat the food, all three cases seem the same.
steps.terutzMaskana: On יום הכפורים, the food was fit for the person before the day began. Wine for a נזיר and תרומה for a ישראל were never fit for them.

steps.title: Whose view does this ברייתא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא this ברייתא follows. It answers that the ברייתא does not follow חנניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom is this? Not in accordance with חנניה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and asks whose opinion the whole ברייתא reflects. It answers right away: not חנניה. This sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, בית שמאי accept a food-based עירוב in principle and only argue about which food qualifies. The גמרא notes that this picture of בית שמאי clashes with חנניה's report of their view.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom?
Not in accordance with חנניה
A תנא who reports a different understanding of בית שמאי's view

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? Not in accordance with Chananya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the debate to identify whose view the ברייתא follows
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's understanding of בית שמאי this ברייתא reflects

steps.title: חנניה's report: בית שמאי require actually moving one's home
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in which חנניה says בית שמאי did not accept a food-based עירוב at all. They required a person to actually move his bed and belongings to the new place.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: חנניה says, the entire view of בית שמאי is that they did not agree to an עירוב at all, until a person takes out his bed and all his household items to there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings חנניה's ברייתא to show why the earlier ברייתא cannot follow him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to חנניה, בית שמאי reject the very idea that placing food can set a new שבת home base. For them, only actually moving your living things there counts. So the whole debate about which food qualifies cannot match חנניה's version of בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Their entire position / their basic view
Agree / accept
His bed
His household items / the things he uses

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to understand בית שמאי. In the main ברייתא, they accept a food עירוב but require food that was fit for the person. According to חנניה, they reject a food עירוב completely and require actually moving one's home.
steps.confusionAlert: חנניה is not adding one more condition to the food עירוב. He is saying בית שמאי do not accept a food עירוב at all.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Chananya says:
The whole (basic) view of Beit Shammai
is that they did not agree to an eiruv (of food)
until he takes out his bed
and all his household items to there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the claim in step 5 that the ברייתא does not follow חנניה
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the ברייתא does not follow חנניה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting חנניה: בית שמאי require actually moving one's bed and belongings, not just placing food

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא about black and white clothing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא about making an עירוב in black or white clothing and asks which תנא it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion does this ברייתא follow? 'If he made an עירוב in black clothes, he may not go out in white. If he made it in white, he may not go out in black.' Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא and asks who taught it. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that the clothing a person wore when he made his עירוב limits which clothing he may go out in. That is a strange rule, since an עירוב is normally about food, not clothing. So the גמרא wants to know which opinion could produce such a rule.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom does this go? (which opinion does it follow?)
That which was taught in a ברייתא
Black (clothes)
White (clothes)

phrases.english: According to whom is that which was taught:
If he made an eiruv in black clothes,
he may not go out in white;
in white, he may not go out in black.
According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on חנניה's view (Step 6) that an עירוב needs one's actual belongings at the new place.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the source of the clothing ברייתא

steps.title: It follows חנניה's version of בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the ברייתא follows חנניה, explaining בית שמאי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is חנניה, following בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The clothing ברייתא follows חנניה's report of what בית שמאי held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חנניה, בית שמאי held that a person's real belongings must be at the new place. So it makes sense that his clothing matters. This links the strange ברייתא to the view the גמרא just quoted in Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who identifies the source
According to (the view of)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is Chananya,
and according to Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: חֲנַנְיָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 7.

steps.title: But חנניה requires all one's belongings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reading. Under חנניה, wearing the 'right' color alone should never be enough, because he requires bringing one's bed and utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to חנניה, is it only in black that he may not go out, but in white he may? Didn't he say an עירוב only works once a person brings his bed and utensils there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. The ברייתא as written does not fit חנניה's strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא implies that clothing alone decides things: wear the same color and you may go. But חנניה said בית שמאי require one's bed and belongings at the new place. Under that view, the right clothing alone could never make an עירוב work.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say?
His bed
His everyday utensils

phrases.english: And according to Chananya,
it is only in black that he may not go out,
but in white he may go out?
But he said: not until he carries out
his bed and his utensils to there!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the attribution in Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The attribution of the clothing ברייתא to חנניה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies the right clothing is enough. חנניה requires all one's belongings, so clothing alone could never be enough.

steps.title: Correcting the ברייתא's wording
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא. If he made the עירוב with white clothes but needed black ones, he may not go out even in white.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: if he made an עירוב with white clothes and then needed black ones, he may not go out even in white.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the ברייתא really means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the new reading, the ברייתא makes things stricter, not more lenient. If a person needs clothing that is not at the עירוב place, then not all his belongings are there. So the עירוב fails completely, and he may not go out even in the white clothes he has. This fits חנניה's requirement exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a corrected reading)
He needed

steps.confusionAlert: In the corrected reading, the ברייתא no longer allows anything. It now says that missing clothing cancels the עירוב entirely, even for the clothes he does have.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
If he made an eiruv in white
and he needed black,
he may not go out even in white.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lets him go out in the same color he wore.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lacking needed clothing at the new place cancels the עירוב entirely, as חנניה requires.

steps.title: The corrected ברייתא is חנניה's view of בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא repeats the attribution, now for the corrected reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is חנניה, following בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא restates its answer. With the corrected wording, the ברייתא clearly follows חנניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating the line confirms that the attribution now fits without problems. The challenge from Step 9 is gone.
steps.whatToRemember: According to חנניה, בית שמאי require all of a person's belongings, even the clothes he needs, to be at the עירוב place. Otherwise the עירוב fails.

phrases.english: According to whom?
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
It is Chananya,
and according to Beit Shammai.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן? אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reaffirms the attribution of Step 8, now for the corrected reading.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The corrected ברייתא follows חנניה's account of בית שמאי.

steps.title: סומכוס disputes תרומה but not a נזיר's wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes סומכוס from the משנה, who requires ordinary food. It notes that he does not argue about wine for a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: סומכוס says: only with ordinary food. Yet about wine for a נזיר, he does not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes סומכוס. This opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה allows an עירוב of wine for a נזיר and of תרומה for a ישראל. סומכוס argues only about תרומה, saying an עירוב must be made with ordinary food. The גמרא notices that he leaves the נזיר case alone, which needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא quoted in the משנה
Ordinary, non-holy food
Whereas; but by contrast
He does not disagree

phrases.english: Summachos says: with non-sacred food.
Whereas regarding a nazir with wine, he does not disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חנניה discussion and returns to the משנה's dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סומכוס requires ordinary food for an עירוב made for a ישראל, but accepts wine for a נזיר.

steps.title: A נזיר can annul his vow
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that a נזיר can ask a חכם to annul his נזירות, and then he could drink the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because he can ask to have his נזירות annulled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why סומכוס treats the נזיר differently and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a נזיר can have his vow released by a חכם, the wine is in his power to make permitted. So it counts as food that is available to him, and the עירוב works.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
He asks (a חכם) to annul a vow
The status of being a נזיר

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is possible for him to ask for annulment of his nazirite vow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the distinction noted in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why סומכוס accepts a נזיר's wine
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The נזיר can have his vow annulled, so the wine is within his reach.

steps.title: Why not annul the תרומה too?
steps.stepSummary: If annulment is the reason, the declaration that made food into תרומה can also be annulled.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should also be possible to ask to annul the תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason it just gave. The same logic should work for תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food becomes תרומה through a spoken declaration, and a חכם can annul such a declaration like a vow. So the ישראל could also make the food permitted to himself, and סומכוס should allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The portion of produce given to a כהן, which a ישראל may not eat

phrases.english: If so,
teruma too,
it is possible to ask for annulment of it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: סומכוס's distinction between a נזיר's wine and תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תרומה declaration can be annulled just like a נזיר's vow.

steps.title: Annulled תרומה becomes טבל
steps.stepSummary: Annulling the תרומה declaration does not help, because the produce goes back to being טבל and is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he annuls it, it goes back to being טבל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Annulment does not make the תרומה permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the תרומה declaration is cancelled, the produce returns to being untithed. Untithed produce, called טבל, is still forbidden to eat. A נזיר's annulment truly permits the wine, but here the food stays forbidden, so סומכוס's distinction holds.

keyTerms.meaning: It returns
Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not been taken; forbidden to eat

steps.whatToRemember: סומכוס accepts a נזיר's wine because annulling the vow really permits it. Annulling a תרומה declaration only turns the food back into forbidden טבל. Steps 16-21 then ask why that טבל cannot be fixed, and step 21 gives the final reason.

phrases.english: If he asks for its annulment,
it returns to being tevel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the two cases are different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Annulment could make תרומה permitted, just as it does a נזיר's wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Annulled תרומה becomes טבל, so the food remains forbidden.

steps.title: Why not separate תרומה for it from other produce?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests fixing the טבל by separating תרומה for it from produce somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him separate תרומה for it from a different place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. If annulling the declaration turns the food back into טבל, he could simply separate תרומה again using other produce, and then the food would be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said annulment does not help, because the food just becomes טבל. But טבל can be fixed by separating תרומה for it. The challenge says: annul, then separate from other produce, and the food becomes permitted חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him separate (תרומה)
Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות were not yet taken; forbidden to eat
From a different place, meaning other produce

phrases.english: Let him separate [תרומה] for it from another place!
phrases.notes: The goal is to fix the טבל after the declaration is annulled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 15 that annulment leaves the food forbidden as טבל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that returning to טבל leaves the food permanently unusable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טבל can be fixed by separating תרומה from other produce, so the food could become permitted.

steps.title: חברים don't separate from produce that isn't nearby
steps.stepSummary: Careful people (חברים) are not suspected of separating תרומה from produce that is not next to the produce being fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: חברים are not suspected of separating תרומה from produce that is not nearby.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that separating from 'another place' is not done to begin with. The proper way is to separate from produce right next to the טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that, ideally, one separates תרומה only from produce that is close by (מוקף). A careful, observant person (a חבר) would not break this rule. So we cannot assume he would fix the food that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Were suspected
People committed to careful observance of מצוות, especially תרומות and מעשרות
Near; produce situated right next to the produce being fixed

phrases.english: חברים are not suspected
of separating תרומה from produce that is not nearby.
phrases.notes: Separating from produce that is not nearby is not done to begin with.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא נֶחְשְׁדוּ חֲבֵירִים לִתְרוֹם שֶׁלֹּא מִן הַמּוּקָּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He could fix the טבל using produce from anywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: Separating from produce that is not nearby is not done to begin with, so this fix is not available.

steps.title: Why not separate from the עירוב food itself?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests separating תרומה from the עירוב food itself, which is certainly nearby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him separate תרומה for it from the food itself!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again. If produce from elsewhere is a problem, he could take the תרומה out of the עירוב food itself, and the rest would be permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking from the food itself solves the 'nearby' issue, since it is the same pile. So the challenge says the remaining food would become permitted to the ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: From it and in it, meaning from the same produce itself

phrases.english: Let him separate [תרומה] for it from the produce itself!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gets around the answer of Step 17 by using the produce itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that separating from elsewhere is not allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separating from the same produce is surely 'nearby', so the food can be fixed.

steps.title: Not enough would be left for an עירוב
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where taking out תרומה would leave less than the required amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where it would not have the required amount.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we are talking about a case where the food is just barely enough for an עירוב. Taking any תרומה out would leave too little.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירוב needs food for two meals. If the food is exactly that amount, removing תרומה drops it below the minimum. Then the עירוב would fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The required amount (here, food for two meals)
There is not in it

phrases.english: Where it does not have the required amount [after separating].
phrases.notes: The leftover would be less than food for two meals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Separating from the food itself always leaves a valid עירוב.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this case the food is exactly the minimum, so separating would leave too little.

steps.title: Why assume such a narrow case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that nothing forces us to say the משנה deals only with this unusual case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what makes it certain that this is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer. Why should we assume the עירוב food is always exactly the minimum amount?
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס gives a general ruling: only חולין, never תרומה. Explaining him through a rare case, where the food is exactly the minimum, is weak. The general ruling needs a general reason.

keyTerms.meaning: What makes it definite? Why assume this specific case across the board?

phrases.english: And what makes it definite [that this is always the case]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the narrow case suggested in Step 19.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general ruling by סומכוס cannot depend on an unusual situation that is not always true.

steps.title: Rabbinic שבת bans already apply at בין השמשות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the earlier answers. סומכוס agrees with the רבנן that anything forbidden as a שבות is forbidden at בין השמשות too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, סומכוס agrees with the רבנן, who say: anything forbidden because of a שבות (a rabbinic שבת ban) was also forbidden at בין השמשות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new, stronger answer that works in every case. The עירוב takes effect at בין השמשות. At that moment it is already forbidden to separate תרומה, so the טבל cannot be fixed then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Separating תרומה on שבת is forbidden by the רבנן (a שבות). The רבנן extended their bans to בין השמשות too. So at the exact moment the עירוב must be usable, the food can never become permitted to a ישראל, however much food there is.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier approach and offers a new one
A שבת prohibition made by the רבנן
Twilight; the doubtful time between day and night
They decreed

steps.whatToRemember: סומכוס forbids a תרומה עירוב for a ישראל for this reason. The עירוב takes effect at בין השמשות, and the רבנן already forbade separating תרומה then. So there is no way to make the food fit for him at that moment.
steps.confusionAlert: The word אֶלָּא means the גמרא is dropping the answers about 'nearby' produce and the minimum amount. The final reason is the twilight ban, not those narrow answers.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that in an עירוב, what counts is the food's status at the moment it takes effect, which is בין השמשות.

phrases.english: Rather, סומכוס agrees with the רבנן
who say: anything
that is [forbidden] because of a rabbinic Shabbat ban
they decreed against it at twilight too.
phrases.notes: So separating תרומה is already forbidden when the עירוב takes effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answers of Steps 17 and 19 with a general reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New general principle replacing earlier answers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: סומכוס's ruling depends on narrow practical problems with separating תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Separating תרומה is banned at בין השמשות, so the food can never be fit for a ישראל when the עירוב takes effect.

steps.title: Whose view says measures depend on each person?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה listing measures that depend on each person's size, including food for an עירוב, and asks whose view it follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view does this משנה follow? 'There are cases where they said everything depends on the person: a handful of a מנחה, two handfuls of incense, one who drinks a cheekful on יום כיפור, and food for two meals for an עירוב.' Whose view is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new question. It cites a משנה saying some measures are set by the individual person's size, and asks which תנא holds that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists four measures that change from person to person, including the two meals for an עירוב. That last item ties back to our topic: whose food standard counts for an עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does it follow?
His handful (the כהן's scoop from a מנחה)
His two cupped hands (the כהן גדול's incense on יום כיפור)
A cheekful; the amount of drinking that makes one liable on יום כיפור
Two meals; the amount of food needed for an עירוב

phrases.english: Whose view does what we learned [in a משנה] follow:
There are [cases] where they said everything
depends on what kind of person he is.
A handful of a meal-offering,
two handfuls of incense,
one who drinks a cheekful
on Yom Kippur,
and food for two meals for an eiruv.
Whose view is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תרומה issue to a related question about whose standard counts for an עירוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that measures, including food for an עירוב, depend on the individual.

steps.title: רבי זירא: it is סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the משנה follows סומכוס, who requires food that is fit for this specific person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: It is סומכוס, who said: we need what is fit for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the question. The משנה matches סומכוס, who judges the עירוב by what is fit for the specific person it serves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס required ordinary food for a ישראל because the food must be fit for him personally (Step 12). The same idea explains the משנה: the two-meal amount is measured by that person's own eating. Both rulings come from one principle: the individual's own fitness and size.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question
What is fit for him
We require

steps.whatToRemember: For סומכוס, an עירוב is measured by the specific person. The food must be fit for him (so no תרומה for a ישראל), and the amount is two meals by his own eating.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
It is [the view of] Summakhos,
who said: we require what is fit for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows סומכוס, who requires food fit for the specific person, so the measures follow the individual.

steps.title: Does this clash with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר about a glutton?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the view requiring food fit for each specific person disagrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. He measures a glutton by an ordinary meal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this disagrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר? A ברייתא teaches that he says: we make an עירוב for a sick or elderly person with the amount of food he actually eats. For a glutton, we use an average meal of a normal person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible problem. If the עירוב measure always follows the specific person, that seems to argue with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who does not follow the glutton's large appetite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that the עירוב amount (two meals) is measured by each person's own eating. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר agrees for a sick or old person, who eats less. But for a big eater he uses the normal amount, not the person's own. So it looks like a disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say it disagrees? (a suggestion that two views clash)
We may make an עירוב
Enough food for him (his own normal amount)
A glutton, a person who eats much more than usual
An average meal

phrases.aramaic: לֵימָא פְּלִיגָא אַדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: Shall we say it disagrees with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar?

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
We make an eruv for a sick or elderly person with enough food for him,
phrases.notes: Even if that is less than a normal person's amount.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְרַעַבְתָן בִּסְעוּדָה בֵּינוֹנִית שֶׁל כׇּל אָדָם!
phrases.english: and for a glutton, with an average meal of an ordinary person!

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא פְּלִיגָא אַדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the conclusion of step 23 against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the עירוב measure follows each specific person (the view of סומכוס).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר does not follow the glutton's own measure, so the measure cannot always be personal.

steps.title: The personal measure applies only to the sick and elderly
steps.stepSummary: The personal measure refers only to a sick or elderly person. A glutton's unusual appetite is ignored, because his standard is cancelled out by everyone else's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain it as referring to a sick or elderly person. But a glutton's view is cancelled out by the view of all people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no disagreement. The 'each person's own measure' rule is meant for people who eat less, like the sick and the elderly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A glutton's huge appetite is abnormal, so the law does not take it into account. His measure is 'בטלה דעתו', set aside in favor of what normal people eat. Everyone can therefore agree with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain it as referring to (a narrowing interpretation)
His standard is cancelled out by that of all people

steps.whatToRemember: The עירוב measure can go down for the sick or elderly, but it never goes up for a glutton. An abnormal appetite is ignored.

phrases.english: Interpret it as referring to a sick or elderly person.
But a glutton, his view is cancelled
in relation to all other people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (the personal measure applies only to sick and elderly people).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The personal measure applies to everyone, gluttons included.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a smaller-than-normal eater gets a personal measure. A glutton is measured by the normal standard.

steps.title: Why a כהן may place his עירוב in a בית הפרס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה allowing a כהן's עירוב in a בית הפרס. It explains this with שמואל's ruling that a person may blow away the dust and walk through.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and for a כהן, an עירוב may be placed in a בית הפרס. This is because רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a person may blow on the dirt of a בית הפרס as he walks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new line of the משנה. It explains why a כהן, who must avoid corpse impurity, can still use an עירוב placed in a בית הפרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הפרס is a field where a grave was plowed over, so bone fragments may be scattered there. That impurity is only a rabbinic rule. Since a person may blow the dirt ahead of him to uncover any bones and walk around them, the כהן is able to reach his עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed, which may contain scattered bone pieces (rabbinic impurity)
A priest, who is forbidden to become impure from a dead body
Blows (on the dirt to uncover bones)

steps.confusionAlert: A בית הפרס is not a real cemetery. Its impurity is rabbinic, and that is why it can be handled this easily.

phrases.english: And for a priest, in a beit haperas.
As Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
A person may blow on a beit haperas and walk on.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַכֹּהֵן בְּבֵית הַפְּרָס. דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining a new clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may use an עירוב in a בית הפרס, because he can blow away the dirt and walk through without becoming impure.

steps.title: A trodden בית הפרס is pure
steps.stepSummary: A second reason the כהן can get there: a בית הפרס that people have walked over is considered pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בר אמי said in the name of רב יהודה: a בית הפרס that has been trampled is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second ruling that also explains how a כהן can reach an עירוב in a בית הפרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once people have walked a path through a בית הפרס, we assume any bone pieces have been crushed or moved away. That path becomes pure. This again shows the impurity here is lenient and rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: That has been trampled (walked over)
Pure

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda bar Ami said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
A beit haperas that has been trampled is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel ruling that supports step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A trampled בית הפרס is pure.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even in a cemetery, because the כהן can travel in a closed box
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה, who allows the עירוב even in a בית הקברות. A ברייתא explains that the כהן can ride inside a carriage, chest, or cupboard.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: even in a cemetery. A ברייתא taught: this is because he can block off the impurity and go inside a carriage, a chest, or a cupboard.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יהודה's view in the משנה, which goes further and allows a כהן's עירוב even in a real cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the impurity comes from the Torah. Blowing on the dirt would not help. But a large container shields whoever is inside it, so a כהן carried in such a box stays pure and can reach his עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: A cemetery (impurity from the Torah)
To block off, place a barrier between himself and the impurity
A carriage, a chest, and a cupboard (large containers)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף בֵּית הַקְּבָרוֹת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: even a cemetery.
It was taught: because he can block off the impurity
and go in a carriage, a chest, or a cupboard.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף בֵּית הַקְּבָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה, which goes further than the בית הפרס case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a כהן may have his עירוב in a cemetery, because he can travel shielded inside a large container.

steps.title: A moving tent counts as a tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that רבי יהודה holds a moving tent is still a tent that blocks impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that a moving tent is called a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the principle that lies behind רבי יהודה's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The carriage or box is moving while the כהן rides in it. Even so, רבי יהודה treats it as a real אהל that blocks impurity from the graves. Someone who does not count a moving tent as a tent would not allow this.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this shows his underlying view)
A moving (lit. thrown) tent

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן may have his עירוב in a בית הפרס because that impurity is rabbinic and avoidable. רבי יהודה allows it even in a cemetery, because he holds that a moving container is a real אהל that shields from impurity.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'אהל זרוק שמיה אהל' is a well-known principle in the laws of טומאה, and other סוגיות discuss it as well.

phrases.aramaic: קָא סָבַר: אֹהֶל זָרוּק שְׁמֵיהּ אֹהֶל.
phrases.english: He holds: a moving tent is called a tent.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָבַר: אֹהֶל זָרוּק שְׁמֵיהּ אֹהֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws out the principle behind step 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה holds that a moving container counts as an אהל, so it protects a כהן from cemetery impurity.

steps.title: A ברייתא where תנאים argue about traveling inside a carriage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the idea of a moving tent is argued about by תנאים. It quotes a ברייתא: someone enters ארץ העמים inside a carriage, chest, or cupboard. רבי says he is impure, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the subject of a dispute between these תנאים, as it was taught in a ברייתא: One who enters the land of the nations in a carriage, a chest, or a cupboard: רבי says he is impure, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the idea from the last step, that a moving tent blocks impurity, to an existing argument between תנאים. It quotes the ברייתא where they argue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חז"ל declared the land outside ארץ ישראל (ארץ העמים) impure. The question is whether sitting inside a moving box protects you from that impurity. רבי says it does not protect you, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it does.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute or argument
תנאים, the Sages of the משנה era
The land of the nations, meaning any land outside ארץ ישראל, which חז"ל declared impure
A carriage, a chest, and a cupboard, all closed containers a person can sit inside
Rules impure / rules pure

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא. He is not the same person as רבי יהודה from the previous step. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is the son of that earlier רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And it is the subject of a dispute between these Tannaim,
phrases.notes: The question of the moving tent was already argued about by תנאים.

phrases.english: as it was taught in a baraita:
One who enters the land of the nations
phrases.notes: Land outside ארץ ישראל, which has rabbinic impurity.

phrases.english: in a carriage, a chest, or a cupboard,
phrases.notes: He is not walking. He is enclosed inside a moving container.

phrases.english: Rabbi (Yehuda HaNasi) renders him impure;
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda renders him pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the conclusion of step 29 (a moving tent is a tent) matches one side of an existing argument between תנאים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who enters ארץ העמים inside a carriage, chest, or cupboard: רבי rules he is impure, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה rules he is pure.

steps.title: What exactly are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies underneath the argument between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the argument. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only gives the two rulings, impure and pure. The גמרא wants the principle that causes each side to rule the way he does.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? This is a standard question asking for the root of an argument.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the argument quoted in step 30.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that separates רבי from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

steps.title: They argue whether a moving tent counts as a tent
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that a moving tent is not a tent, so the person inside becomes impure. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that a moving tent is a tent, so the person inside stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage (רבי) holds that a moving tent is not called a tent. The other Sage (רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה) holds that a moving tent is called a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the whole argument depends on אהל זרוק, a tent that is moving.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal tent blocks impurity from reaching the person inside it. רבי says a box that is moving is not a real tent, so it gives no protection. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it does count as a tent and protects the person inside. This matches the view the גמרא gave for רבי יהודה in step 29.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'thrown' or moving tent, meaning a covering that is in motion and not fixed in place
One Sage holds
It is called a tent, meaning it has the legal status of a tent

steps.whatToRemember: The question of אהל זרוק is an argument between תנאים. רבי says it is not a tent, while רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, and also רבי יהודה, say it is a tent and blocks impurity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יהודה's ruling, which lets the כהן reach his עירוב in a בית הקברות by riding in a box, is based on a known position. It is not a strange new idea.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר אֹהֶל זָרוּק לָאו שְׁמֵיהּ אֹהֶל,
phrases.english: One Sage holds a moving tent is not called a tent,
phrases.notes: That's רבי's view, so the person inside becomes impure.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר אֹהֶל זָרוּק שְׁמֵיהּ אֹהֶל.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds a moving tent is called a tent.
phrases.notes: That's רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view, so the person inside stays pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר אֹהֶל זָרוּק לָאו שְׁמֵיהּ אֹהֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 31.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They argue about whether an אהל זרוק has the status of a tent that blocks impurity.

steps.title: Introducing another teaching from רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to bring up another ברייתא in the name of רבי יהודה, which it will discuss next.
steps.simpleTranslation: And regarding that which was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to quote a different ברייתא from רבי יהודה, and it will discuss that ברייתא on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase והא דתניא tells us the גמרא is about to deal with a source that may seem to clash with, or need to be fit into, what was just said about רבי יהודה. The actual content of that source comes in the following text.

keyTerms.meaning: And that which was taught in a ברייתא. It introduces a source the גמרא is about to discuss.

phrases.english: And that which was taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
phrases.notes: The content of the ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After establishing רבי יהודה's view on a moving tent, the גמרא turns to another ברייתא in his name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An introductory line. The ruling itself appears on the next amud.
